THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

By the consent of learned counsel for both the sides, the matters are taken up for final disposal,
though they are posted for Admission.

These appeals by the petitioner as well as by the KSRTC are directed against the judgment and award passed in MVC No.1012/2016 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Hassan,
dated 9-2-2018 whereby, the Tribunal awarded compensation of `9,60,000/- to the petitioner on account of the death of the son of petitioner.

2. The petitioner contended that on 6-5-2016 her son Madhusudhana and her son-in-law were proceeding towards Shantigrama on the motor cycle with her son as the pillion rider, and while her son was crossing the road near Kasthuravalli gate, the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.13.F.2140 came from Hassan side in rash NC: 2023:KHC:21487 and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle resulting in the death of Madhusudhana on the spot.
Petitioner had to spend for the obsequies and she has lost her dependency and that the deceased was earning `50,000/- per month by doing ginger selling business.
Therefore, she claimed adequate compensation from the respondents.

3. On issuance of notice, the respondent-KSRTC appeared before the Tribunal and filed its objections denying the age, occupation and income of the deceased and contended that there was no such negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus and the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable in law.
It also contended that an exgratia of `15,000/- was paid by the respondent-KSRTC on humanitarian grounds.
Therefore, the respondent sought dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner was NC: 2023:KHC:21487 examined as PW1 and Exs.P1 to P9 were marked and one witness was examined as PW2.

The driver of the KSRTC bus was examined as RW1 and Exs.R1 to 5 were marked.
5.

After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal awarded a compensation of `9,60,000/- by adopting a notional income of `7,000/- and multiplier of 15, under following heads:
Loss of dependency `8,40,000/-
Transportation of dead body and ` 25,000/-
miscellaneous charges Loss of love and affection ` 50,000/-
Loss of consortium ` 10,000/-
Loss of estate ` 10,000/-
Funeral and obsequies expenses ` 25,000/-
Total ` 9,60,000/-

3
6. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner as well as the respondent -KSRTC have come up in these appeals.
7. The petitioner contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager, low and the notional income was not properly considered by the Tribunal.

It is contended that the Tribunal has not considered the NC: 2023:KHC:21487 adequate and just compensation and as such, there is a need for enhancement.
8.

Per contra, the respondent-KSRTC in its appeal contends that the deceased was a pillion rider on the motor cycle and at about 5.30 a.m. they stopped their motor cycle by the side of the road and when the deceased was crossing the road to go for a nature call, the accident has happened.

It is contended that there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and therefore, the Tribunal erred in holding that there was no such contributory negligence.
9.
On issuance of notice, the rival parties have appeared through their counsels and on admitting the appeal, the Tribunal records have been secured.
10. At the instance of both the counsels, the appeals are heard together and perused the records.
11. A perusal of the Tribunal records would show that the deceased as well as the rider of the motors cycle NC: 2023:KHC:21487 Shantharaju were traveling on the motor cycle at about 5.30 a.m.
The said Shantharaju, the rider, was examined as PW2.

He states that he was riding the motorcycle and at the request of the deceased, he stopped the motor cycle and while the deceased was crossing the Hasana- Bengaluru High way, the bus belonging to the respondent- KSRTC dashed against the deceased Madhusudhana and he died at the spot.
He says that the accident was due to the negligence of the bus driver but not due to the negligence of the deceased.
It is evident that accident had happened at about 5.30 a.m.
The police have investigated the matter and filed chargesheet against the bus driver.

A perusal of the investigating papers as well as the evidence of the driver of the bus would show that it is a straight road and the deceased could have seen the vehicle coming from either directions.
It was a four lane high way and there was no pedestrian crossing at the place of the accident.
The evidence also discloses that the deceased had not seen the bus coming towards Shantigrama and had tried to cross the road.
Obviously, the bus which was NC: 2023:KHC:21487 in speed could not be stopped by RW1 which resulted in the accident.
Considering the above circumstance, it is evident that the Tribunal was not justified in attributing negligence entirely to RW1.

In view of the circumstance that the bus driver was in full view of the stopping of the motor cycle and the deceased trying to cross the road, should also have taken adequate precautions in slowing down the bus.
Hence, the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is prima facie evident from the records available.
In the opinion of this Court, such contributory negligence is to the extent of 10%.
12. Obviously, the petitioner has not proved the income of the deceased to be `50,000/- per month as claimed by her and therefore, the Tribunal was justified in adopting the notional income.
The Tribunal holds such income to be `7,000/- per month.
The guidelines by the KSLSA for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalaths prescribe the notional income of `9,500/- for the year 2016.

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation head of loss of dependency is calculated as: `13,300(`9,500/- + `3,800/-) x 12 x 15 x 50% = `11,97,000/- by adopting future prospects at 40% and multiplier of 15 for the age of 38 years and deducting personal expenses at 50% for he being a bachelor.
13. In addition to the above quantum, a sum of `48,400/- is to be added towards the loss of love and affection, `18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus, the total compensation would be `12,81,700/-.
The contributory negligence of the deceased was to the extent of 10% and therefore, after deduction of the same, the entitlement of the petitioner would be `11,97,000/-.
Respondent KSRTC has already paid a sum of `15,000/- as interim compensation.
After deduction of the same, the net entitlement of the petitioner would `11,38,530/-.

Hence, the entitlement of the petitioner would be as below:
- 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC:21487 Loss of dependency ` 11,97,000/-
Loss of love and affection ` 48,400/-
Loss of estate ` 18,150/-
Funeral expenses ` 18,150/-
Total ` 12,81,700/-
Less:10% towards contributory negligence ` 1,28,170/-
Total compensation ` 11,53,530/-
Less: `15,000/- awarded by KSRTC as ` 15,000/-
interim relief Total entitlement by petitioner ` 11,38,530/-
Less: Awarded by Tribunal ` 9,60,000/-
 ` 1,78,530/-
14.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of `1,78,530/- together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Both the appeals are allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1012/2016 dated 9-2-2018 is modified by fixing the contributory negligence of the deceased at 10% and by enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal to `12,81,700/-.

(iv) Respondent-KSRTC is directed to deposit the compensation amount within six weeks from today.
(v) The other conditions regarding the fixed deposit remain unaltered.
